text: Varicella-zoster virus (VZV), a neurotropic and epidermotropic herpesvirus, causes varicella (chickenpox) upon primary infection and reactivates later in life to cause herpes zoster (HZ), which is associated with significant morbidity, particularly postherpetic neuralgia (PHN). VZV genotyping and characterization of key viral proteins, such as glycoprotein E (gE), are critical for understanding viral circulation, distinguishing vaccine from wild-type strains, and optimizing vaccine strategies. In China, clade 2 is the predominant VZV genotype, but data from Shanxi Province remain limited.
source_label: Analysis of the genotyping of circulating strains and characteristics of Glycoprotein E of Varicella-Zoster Virus in Shanxi Province, China
